productFit.name: Apple HomePod mini 2
productFit.reason: Apple's own NL spec page lists HomePod mini 2 with a 20 W adapter in the box (Netspanning 100-240 V wisselstroom, 50-60 Hz), Wi-Fi 6E, Thread, temperature and humidity sensor, and HomeKit / Home app support. Mains is 230 V compatible, so no converter is needed. Caveat for the post: the ASIN is carried from the existing German speaker post and is unverified for the EU Amazon store; the post should send readers to the NL Apple Store / EU retailer listing by name, not to a US import, because the adapter plug differs by region.

productFit.name: Apple TV 4K (4th generation)
productFit.reason: Apple's NL spec page lists the 128 GB model with A19 chip, Wi-Fi 7, Gigabit Ethernet, Thread, HDMI 2.1, built-in power supply with power cord in the box, Netspanning 100-240 V wisselstroom, 50-60 Hz. Works as a home hub. No ASIN in the English post (amzn query only). Needs a HDMI cable sold separately. Apple's support page notes HomePod mini, HomePod and Apple TV are not available in all countries, but both pages are live on Apple NL.

localFacts.fact: Apple's Dutch support page uses 'woninghub' and the 'Woning-app': a woninghub must be set up to add Matter accessories, Thread-capable Matter accessories need a Thread-capable woninghub (HomePod mini or Apple TV 4K 3rd gen Wi-Fi + Ethernet, or a supported third-party border router), and only the Home's owner can add HomePod or Apple TV as hub.

Apple's Dutch spec pages list HomePod mini 2 (20 W adapter, 100-240 V, 50-60 Hz) and Apple TV 4K (4th gen, 100-240 V, netsnoer included), so both work on Dutch/Belgian 230 V sockets. The HomePod mini 2 page lists Dutch radio (Qmusic, Radio 538, Radio 2, Radio 10).

The Dutch government (Rijksoverheid) says a tenant may make small changes that can be reversed without too much cost without the landlord's permission, while renovation always needs the landlord's permission; the Juridisch Loket covers leaving a rental in its original state. Plug-in hubs fall under no changes at all.

iCulture (Dutch Apple site) says renters can place smart lamps, cameras, motion sensors and plugs easily, but that adding to heating installations or built-in switches needs the owner's permission, and that a smart doorbell or lock is often not worth it or not even allowed in a rental.

Dutch Apple coverage (iCulture, Tweakers) reports Apple announced new Home products on 13 October 2026 (HomeView display, Apple Home Collection); the English post does not mention this, so the localized post may want a neutral 'check what Apple has launched' line.

localPainPoints.pain: Hub reliability on wifi: Tweakers HomeKit forum users report that a wired Apple TV should work better than a HomePod on wifi.
localPainPoints.fix: Use the English post's wired Apple TV 4K advice (Gigabit Ethernet) and the restart-the-hub order; mention the Apple Dutch page's step to check the hub is on the home wifi.

localPainPoints.pain: Which device can be the hub: Tweakers readers still ask whether an old iPad can serve; a Tweakers news thread notes Apple said iPads would stop acting as hub.
localPainPoints.fix: State that the hub is a HomePod, HomePod mini or Apple TV (Apple's Dutch page still lists iPad only in the update/restart steps), so a renter needs one of the two products in the post.
